summary: Jambi stands under Indonesia's national framework, which the parent record carries in full. The sources identify no Jambi-specific finding: no provincial or district-level ordinance addressing same-sex conduct or gender expression, no local anti-discrimination protection, and no documented incident involving a trans person in the province. A trans visitor to Jambi therefore faces the national assessment without local modification, and no Jambi institution, regulation or enforcement practice altering it was found.
tangentialFactors:
The enforcement actions the inventory records, among them a police raid on a private gathering and arrests over a social-media page, took place outside Jambi; the province is not the location of any documented case. The sources give no counts broken down by province for incidents or prosecutions, so Jambi cannot be ranked against other Indonesian provinces, and national totals would not describe conditions there.

The inventory offers no basis for comparing Jambi with provinces that have their own ordinances, and it records no public statement by Jambi officials, no local religious-authority campaign and no provincial enforcement trend.
localsOnly:
No Jambi-specific rule governing residents was identified. The province has no ordinance on gender expression or dress, no local anti-discrimination or employment protection on grounds of gender identity, and no provincial procedure or office handling legal gender recognition. Residents of Jambi stand under the national rules carried by the parent record, and no Jambi institution is documented as applying them differently.

No reporting in the sources documents violence, harassment or police action against trans residents of Jambi, and no local facility, shelter or complaint mechanism specific to the province is described.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Jambi finding rests on a single national-level source inventory. No Jambi-specific reporting, no text of provincial or district local regulations (perda), and no local news monitoring were available, so the absence of a local ordinance is unresolved rather than confirmed against the province's regulation register.

Whether public-order or religious-affairs officers conduct enforcement against gender-nonconforming people anywhere in Jambi is not sourced. No province-level data on policing, facilities access, healthcare availability or hate-crime reporting for trans visitors was identified, and the national figures carried by the parent record are not broken down by province.
